subject: Provisional capacity credit swap + pricing schedule clarifications
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <tay@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional capacity credit swap + pricing schedule clarifications

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Following up with a concrete path we discussed on the call: Redwood is willing to exchange a tranche of provisional capacity credits in Q3 for a short-term smoothing of the pricing floor in Q4 (we intend this purely as a temporary accommodation while you ramp usage).

Key bullets (attached: ACME_Capacity_Credits_Schedule_v3.pdf and a first-pass markup):
- Credits: 200k token credits, applied monthly as a line-item credit on invoices for Jul–Sep 2027.
- Swap mechanics: if actual usage exceeds the provisional credits, normal per-token rates apply; if below, unused credits do not roll forward.
- Pricing floor adjustment: reduce Q4 floor from $45k to $35k for one quarter contingent on signing the attached exhibit amendment.
- Make-up clause: if Q1 2028 usage is below the original commit, Redwood proposes a scaled make-up true-up over two quarters rather than an immediate true-up.

I attached a redline for Exhibit C that overlays these changes. This should keep procurement happy in the near-term while protecting Redwood revenue. Can you confirm whether Acme can accept the temporary floor reduction and the make-up mechanism? If so, we can route the amended exhibit to legal for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Also CC'ing Karthik for legal language on the make-up and Marissa for finance to confirm billing triggers.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Provisional capacity credit swap + pricing schedule clarifications

Jonas —

Appreciate the detailed note. The team is supportive of a temporary floor reduction but we need two clarifications before legal will greenlight: (1) exact invoice treatment of the provisional credits (line item vs. bill offsets) and (2) concrete example calculations so procurement can see the monthly cadence and the effect on our cash flow.

Two asks: can you send an example invoice month showing the credit applied and a worked example that shows the Q4 floor at $35k vs $45k? Also, the make-up over two quarters sounds okay but we need to ensure it doesn't create a large lump-sum true-up that requires us to pre-fund.

I attached Acme's standard procurement schedule for reference. We can schedule a 20 min call next week if that's easier.

Thanks,
Taylor

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional capacity credit swap + pricing schedule clarifications

Taylor / Jonas —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the proposed Exhibit C redline and added tracked-comments in exhibit_C_redline_jonas_karthik.docx (attached). High-level legal points below:

1) Invoice treatment: we should explicitly state that provisional credits will appear as a separate credit line on the monthly invoice and carry a unique credit id; credits will be consumed in chronological order. This avoids ambiguity on whether credits reduce the base charge or are classified as refunds.

2) Make-up mechanics: instead of a blunt two-quarter amortization, propose a sliding make-up where the true-up is capped at 50% of the difference in any given quarter with the remainder amortized the following quarter. This prevents a single large lump-sum.

3) Cap/floor language: redline replaces the absolute phrase "temporary" with a fixed term ("for the quarter commencing 1 Oct 2027"), so both parties have a measurable end date. Also inserted language allowing Redwood to revert the floor earlier if usage materially exceeds the provisional credits (materiality threshold: >120% of credits used in a single month).

4) Audit & reporting: require a monthly usage statement with 10 business day dispute window; after that window the invoice is final.

If Acme is comfortable with the sliding true-up and the explicit invoice treatment, we can prepare the final amendment and route to DocuSign. Jonas — if you want, I can convert the tracked comments to clean contract wording for signature.

Karthik

--

Thanks Karthik, that sliding make-up looks like a good compromise. Taylor — can you confirm Acme is OK with: (A) credits listed as a separate invoice line, (B) the sliding make-up cap at 50% per quarter, and (C) the explicit quarter end date (1 Oct 2027) for the temporary floor? If yes, I will ask Marissa to approve billing triggers and then we can route to DocuSign.

If preferable, I can also push a worked example for you by EOD — would that help procurement?

Jonas

- DocuSign: once legal signs off, send to finance@redwood.com and we will push the first credit on the Jul invoice cycle (cutoff is 25 Jun).
- Please include a worked example showing the monthly charge, credit deduction, and the amortized true-up for transparency — procurement asked specifically for a month-by-month illustration.

Action items:
1) Jonas: add exhibit_C_redline_jonas_karthik.docx to https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-12345 and confirm.
2) Karthik: convert tracked comments to final contract language for Exhibit C.
3) Taylor: confirm you accept the invoice treatment + sliding make-up.

Once we have confirmations, we'll route to DocuSign (link will be shared on the HubSpot deal).

Marissa
